122	
123	| file | rows | look-ahead status |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| `bars` | every bar | `i, datetime, date, session_idx, session_bar, open, high, low, close, volume, oi, contract, expiry, front_month, fm_na, atr14, prot` (the protected level as of the bar), `vol_med20_prior, vol_ratio20, vol_ratio60, sess_cumvol, sess_cumvol_ratio20s, split`: all as-of |

content.content:
1	# FZ v3 study brief (2026-09-29): can the bands skip losers without skipping winners?
2	
3	User's words (verbatim intent): "bands exist to take me to profit not to loss; it should avoid only loss trades and not profitable ones; it's different for different time. Check how price reacts in visibly high volume. Those levels will be respected: if it breaks there will be a large move, else price retests, retests and respects. Use reinforcement learning and generative AI to figure out how to arrive at these. My observation: if CHoCH and CHoCH and no breaks then it's sideways; trades in sideways are hurting."
4	
5	State of the lab (research/strategy_lab): Foundation engine (engine.py, untouched), FZ base ST5/ST6 (band model), FZ v2 rooms ST7/ST8 (frozen, accepted 2026-09-28; see FZ.md §19). Strategies 9-12 belong to another session ("Buy only"): managed exits and stop-and-reverse. Next free numbers for FZ v3 are ST13 (1 min) and ST14 (5 min); reserved with that session. Data: config/data.json now points at 5-year near-month files: futures D:/nifty/niftyfut_nearmonth_minute_2021-10-01_to_2026-09-25.csv and the 5-minute sibling, index nifty50_breeze_* (spot has no usable volume). front_month is 1 on every row (volume live everywhere). 1,188 sessions in the files. NOTE (user decision 2026-09-29, relayed by the Buy only session): config/data.json now has "history_from": "2026-01-01" and lab.sessions() ignores earlier sessions, so the lab dashboard "All data" is 5 Jan - 25 Sep 2026 (162 sessions, the May 2026 contract still missing) and the lab FZ memory starts 1 Jan 2026. The data files are unchanged; this study reads them in full through engine.load, never through lab.sessions(). The published lab window therefore coincides with this study OOS window. A full lab rebuild by the other session is running under cache/lab.lock (the file always exists; check for a running `python lab.py` process instead); do not run lab.py, do not write into the repo; everything goes to the session scratchpad.
6	
7	## Protocol (pre-registered before any number is looked at)
8	- IS (learning / hypothesis) = sessions 2021-10-01 .. 2025-12-31. OOS (confirmation, touched once at the end) = 2026-01-01 .. 2026-09-25. Nothing chosen on OOS. Report both, always with the session-matched random control (fz_report.random_control) and the kept-vs-refused permutation p.
9	- Unit of analysis = Foundation SETUP with its own Foundation trade outcome (pts, net at 65 lot, exit reason) from engine.run with the ST1 rules on 1m (touch, prev_swing) and ST2 rules on 5m (touch, choch_candle). A "gate" is any rule that turns a SETUP into skip; a gate is judged by: net of kept, net of skipped, share of winners skipped (recall of losers vs precision), and the control percentile.
10	- Every candidate rule must be expressible as a compact config (thresholds, a rule list of at most 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3), because the lab forbids trading numbers in code; provenance = "learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha".
11	- Costs: charges + slippage = 1,114 INR per 1m trade; any gate that trades less raises net. Selection = kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference and the control percentile, never net alone.
12	- Look-ahead: every feature at a SETUP bar uses bars <= that bar only; forward returns are labels, never features. State it per feature.
13	
14	## Hypotheses to test (each an agent)
15	H1 Gate audit: what do ST7/ST8 (rooms, frozen rules) and ST5/ST6 skip? Split skipped SETUPs by Foundation outcome (win/loss, pts buckets), by hour bin, by read, by block reason. Does the gate skip losers more than winners (precision/recall)? Where does it skip the big winners (the "late runners" the user saw)? Same on IS and OOS.
16	H2 Sideways = CHoCH without break: define regime per bar from engine events: n_choch_since_bos (CHoCHs since the last BOS), n_bos_since_choch, bars_since_choch, alternation count in the last K events, and the range of the last N bars vs ATR. Foundation P&L by regime, per timeframe, per hour. Does "CHoCH, CHoCH, no BOS" mark losing trades? Test a regime filter (skip SETUPs when n_choch_since_bos >= k) on IS, confirm on OOS, with control percentile.
17	H3 Visibly high volume: define a bar as visibly high volume when volume >= v x median volume of the last N bars (grid v in 2,3,4; N in 20,60), same session. Measure price reaction after such bars (forward 5/15/30 bar returns and MAE/MFE, direction relative to the bar's close vs open), whether the bar's high/low holds for the next N bars, and Foundation outcomes for SETUPs within M bars after a high-volume bar, by direction agreement.
18	H4 Levels respected or broken: for protected levels and room edges (ST7 rooms card) and swing highs/lows: at each touch, measure follow-through: break (close beyond by > x ATR within N bars) vs retest/respect (return inside). Distribution of the move size after a confirmed break vs after a respect. Number of retests before a break. Foundation SETUPs taken at a respected level vs at a broken level: outcomes. Is "retests, retests, respects" measurable and does it predict?
19	H5 Learned gate (offline contextual bandit / supervised): build the per-SETUP feature table (card fields from fz.run with ST7/ST8 config, regime features from H2, volume features from H3, level context from H4, hour, gap, session_bar, direction, ATR, Foundation SL distance). Label = Foundation net > 0 (and pts). On IS: (a) a depth-<=3 decision tree and a greedy rule-list search (exhaustive single/pair thresholds) for rules that skip losers with minimal winner loss; (b) a gradient boosting reference (sklearn is installed: 1.7.2) for the ceiling. Choose by IS cross-validation only. Evaluate once on OOS: kept net vs raw vs random control, precision/recall on losers, calibration. Output the winning rule list as JSON config candidate for ST13/ST14. State why sequential RL is not justified (one-step decision, ~2k-6k SETUPs) and how this is a contextual bandit.
20	
21	## Data build (shared, first)
22	One agent per timeframe writes to scratchpad/fz_v3/<tf>/: bars with session index, engine output (setups, chs, events incl. BOS, prot, swings), Foundation trades with pts/net/exit (net = pts x 65 minus 1,114 INR costs for 1m, minus 5-minute-appropriate costs: use lab.trade_charges with ZERODHA_NFO_FUT and slippage 5 pts per side), fz.run card + ledger with the ST7 (1m) / ST8 (5m) fz block (thresholds from strategies/strategy_7.json / strategy_8.json), and the feature table per SETUP (columns documented in a README.md next to the files). Use engine.load on the whole file, then fz_exec.view, lab.fm_by_day-equivalent (front_month from the CSV), atr14 via lab.atr_series; do not run lab.py. Save as CSV (+ parquet if pandas is present). Record run times.
23	
24	## Deliverable per study agent
25	Structured findings with numbers on IS and OOS separately, the exact definition of every feature and rule, the control percentile for any gate, and a candidate config (JSON) if the hypothesis survives. Adversarial refuters then check leakage, definitions, arithmetic and OOS discipline.
26	
27	## Addendum (2026-09-29, user instructions after the first launch)
28	
29	1. **"Ensure to use latest AI and machine-learning techniques to understand the patterns and come up with how to trade in this."** The classical H1-H5 program above is the floor, not the ceiling. A design panel (three lenses: quant-ML canon, sequence/representation learning, decision-making/RL; two judges) selected the modern studies; its output is `DESIGN_PANEL.md` next to this file and is part of the program. The final deliverable is a trading playbook: which Foundation SETUPs to take or skip by regime / time / volume / level context, how to size, how to exit, with out-of-sample evidence and the random control.
30	2. **"You can use it to figure out the patterns and code in this as well."** Survivors are coded into the lab as new strategies ST13 (1 min) and ST14 (5 min) (`strategies/strategy_13.json`, `strategy_14.json`, reserved and confirmed free with the other sessions on 2026-09-29; list the folder again before creating them). ST5-ST8 stay frozen; nothing in `engine.py` changes; no trading number in code (every threshold, weight file path and learner hyper-parameter is a strategy-file key with a `source`).
31	3. **"Ensure not to take shortcuts or skip best analysis or modelling or training due to hardware constraint; if that's the call then move to Claude cloud by committing required files."** The four input files are committed under `fz_v3/data/` for that reason. In the cloud: install what the program needs (xgboost, shap, torch, hmmlearn, stumpy, statsmodels, mapie ... as the design calls for), use every core, and run the full grids, bootstraps and training schedules the design specifies; never shrink a model or a resample count to fit a box.
32	4. **"Even incorporate journal every trade and induce reinforcement learning after each trade to optimize strategy, money management and profit factor."** Two requirements:
33	   - **Trade journal.** One row per Foundation SETUP (taken or skipped) and per closed trade: timestamp, direction, the full feature vector at the decision bar (card fields, regime, volume, level context, time), the policy's decision and its stated reason, the policy's state id (which model / which update it was made with), fill, exit reason, MFE / MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R-multiple, and the running book (equity, drawdown, rolling profit factor). This journal is the training set of the online learner and the audit trail of every decision. In the lab build it is a table the strategy writes (`fz_journal.csv` or a `journal` block in the results), never a side effect hidden in code.
34	   - **Learning after each trade (online / walk-forward).** The policy used at trade t is fitted only on journal rows of trades closed before t (strictly causal; anchored or rolling window as a config key), and is refitted after every closed trade (or every k trades, k a key). Actions: take / skip and position size (lots, bounded by a money-management rule such as fractional Kelly on the calibrated win probability and the expected R, with a maximum lots key and a daily loss stop key). Reward: net P&L per trade with the objective reported as net, profit factor (gross wins / gross losses), max drawdown and the kept-vs-skipped expectancy; because profit factor is not additive, the learner optimises a per-trade surrogate (net, or net with an asymmetric loss penalty) and the policy is *selected* on walk-forward profit factor. Candidate learners, all to be run and compared: contextual bandits with exploration (LinUCB / Thompson sampling on a logistic or tree-embedded model), online gradient-boosted refits, and an offline-RL exit policy (fitted Q-iteration / conservative Q-learning over bar-by-bar in-trade states with doubly-robust off-policy evaluation). Evaluate the whole walk-forward path on IS (learning curve: after how many trades does the policy beat "take everything" and the random control?) and then once on OOS with the learner continuing to update through OOS exactly as it would live. Compare against the static IS-fitted model and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate.
35	   - The lab strategy that results carries the learner as config (algorithm, features, update cadence, priors, sizing keys, provenance), with a **deterministic, replayable** update path from the journal, so that a rerun over the same tape reproduces the same decisions bit for bit.
36	5. **"Take all required data to cloud and start from scratch if any compromise has happened in the study here."** The cloud run is the authoritative run and starts from scratch: rebuild both datasets from `fz_v3/data/` with no memory or process limits, rerun every study, and use `fz_v3/built/` (the local build, made under a 1 GB / 2-process limit and interrupted once by a session restart) only as a cross-check of SETUP counts, Foundation trades and the room card — never as an input. Any local number that the cloud rebuild does not reproduce is discarded, and the difference is recorded in `fz_v3/out/QUALITY.md`. Data in the repo: the four futures / spot files only. The options directories (`D:/nifty/data`, `D:/nifty/options`, several GB) are not in the repo, so the cloud runs the futures books (the gate lives on the futures tape); option-type books for ST13/ST14 are produced by the lab on the local machine after the cloud commits are pulled.
37	6. **Coordination with the other lab session ("Buy only").** Their strategies 19-24 (`rl.py`, `entry_rule rl_v1`) are a contextual bandit (Bayesian linear regression per action, Thompson sampling) that chooses, at each Foundation SETUP, skip or an exit profile x stop x lots from Foundation-side features, with full-information updates in exit-time order, learning from Oct 2021 onward. FZ v3 does not duplicate that: v3 decides take / skip from room, regime, volume, level and time context with its own journal and online learner; for the exit / size stage compose with `rl.py` where it exists (or a config-level reference to it) rather than building a second bandit, and say so in the strategy files. ST15-ST18 are their positional exit variants; do not touch strategies 9-12 and 15-24.

1	"""Study ext_features: the extended as-of scalar features the design panel hands to the importance study (and nothing else).
2	
3	    python build_ext.py --tf minute   --data ../../data/minute                         --out ../../features_ext/minute
4	    python build_ext.py --tf minute   --data ../../data/minute/trunc_20250630_120000   --out ../../features_ext/minute/trunc_20250630_120000
5	
6	Writes <out>/ext_features_all.parquet (one row per SETUP of <data>/features.parquet, keyed by setup_i; every candidate column,
7	before the truncation diff) and <out>/ext_fit_report.json (d*, ADF tables, BOCPD priors, state means, jump lambda, timings, coverage).
8	
9	Sources (DESIGN_PANEL.md, judges' fixes binding): quant-ml-canon-feature-importance (FFD), quant-ml-canon-regime-breaks (BSADF,
10	CUSUM filter, CSW; features only, no gate), deep-sequence-regime-states (BOCPD, GMM, forward-filtered HMM, jump model; features
11	only, no tau grid), deep-sequence-motif-shapelet (nn_dist_prefix / p1_dist_prefix only), deep-sequence-rocket-probe (three window
12	scalars only). Hindsight proxies (deep-sequence-vision-labels) are labels and are not computed here.
13	
14	Fit window for every unsupervised fit and every z-scoring statistic: the IS bars of sessions 2021-10-01 .. 2023-09-30 (the first
15	IS half). Label-free. The second IS half and OOS never enter a fit; inference is a forward pass over the whole tape from bar 0
16	with the frozen model. Every feature at SETUP bar k uses bars <= k.
17	"""

273	def _novelty_batch(close, ks, ms):
274	    import numpy as np, stumpy
275	    out = np.full((len(ks), 2 * len(ms)), np.nan)
276	    for q, k in enumerate(ks):
277	        for j, m in enumerate(ms):
278	            if k - m < m: continue                                        # the prefix must hold at least one m-bar subsequence
279	            T = close[:k - m]                                            # bars 0 .. k-m-1: strictly before k-m
280	            Q = close[k - m + 1:k + 1]
281	            if np.std(Q) <= 0: continue
282	            d = stumpy.mass(Q, T)
283	            d = d[np.isfinite(d)]
284	            if len(d) == 0: continue
285	            out[q, 2 * j] = float(np.min(d)); out[q, 2 * j + 1] = float(np.quantile(d, 0.01))
286	    return out

1	"""Numba kernels and helpers for the extended as-of features (study ext_features). Every kernel reads bars <= t only.
2	
3	Conventions shared by build_ext.py:
4	  * "gap-free log return" r_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}) except at a session's first bar, where r_t = log(close_t / open_t),
5	    so the overnight gap never enters a return-based statistic (the dataset README's convention for windows).
6	  * same-session windows: a window of N bars ending at t is cut at the session's first bar s0 = t - session_bar[t].
7	"""
8	import math
9	import numpy as np
10	from numba import njit
11	
12	NAN = np.nan
13	
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- returns and per-bar helpers
16	@njit(cache=True)
17	def gapfree_logret(close, open_, session_bar):
18	    n = close.shape[0]; r = np.empty(n)
19	    for t in range(n):
20	        if t == 0 or session_bar[t] == 0: r[t] = math.log(close[t] / open_[t])
21	        else: r[t] = math.log(close[t] / close[t - 1])
22	    return r

25	def ffd_weights(d, thres=1e-4):
26	    """Fixed-width fractional-differentiation weights (AFML 5.5): w_0 = 1, w_k = -w_{k-1} (d - k + 1) / k, cut when |w_k| < thres."""
27	    w = [1.0]; k = 1
28	    while True:
29	        wk = -w[-1] * (d - k + 1) / k
30	        if abs(wk) < thres: break
31	        w.append(wk); k += 1
32	    return np.array(w)
33	
34	
35	def ffd_series(y, w):
36	    """x_t = sum_j w_j y_{t-j} (direct convolution, so x_t depends on y_{t-L+1..t} only and is exact for any tape length); NaN for t < L-1."""
37	    L = len(w)
38	    x = np.convolve(y, w, mode="full")[:len(y)]
39	    x[:L - 1] = NAN
40	    return x

43	@njit(cache=True)
44	def rolling_z(x, win):
45	    """(x_t - mean(x_{t-win+1..t})) / std(x_{t-win+1..t}) (ddof 1), NaN until win values are available or when any is NaN."""
46	    n = x.shape[0]; out = np.full(n, NAN)
47	    for t in range(win - 1, n):
48	        s = 0.0; s2 = 0.0; ok = True
49	        for j in range(t - win + 1, t + 1):
50	            v = x[j]
51	            if v != v: ok = False; break
52	            s += v; s2 += v * v
53	        if not ok: continue
54	        m = s / win; var = (s2 - win * m * m) / (win - 1)
55	        if var > 1e-300: out[t] = (x[t] - m) / math.sqrt(var)
56	    return out

59	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BSADF (Phillips, Shi & Yu 2015 backward SADF) at a bar
60	@njit(cache=True)
61	def _adf_t_from_sums(xtx, xty, yty, nrows):
62	    """t-statistic of the y_{t-1} coefficient (index 1) of dy = X b + e from accumulated normal-equation sums."""
63	    if nrows <= 5: return NAN
64	    inv = np.linalg.inv(xtx)
65	    b = inv @ xty
66	    rss = yty - b @ xty
67	    if rss <= 0: return NAN
68	    s2 = rss / (nrows - 4)
69	    v = s2 * inv[1, 1]
70	    if v <= 0: return NAN
71	    return b[1] / math.sqrt(v)

74	@njit(cache=True)
75	def bsadf_at(logc, k, W, mmin):
76	    """Backward SADF at bar k: max over start s of the ADF t-statistic (constant + y_{t-1} + 2 lags of dy) on log close over
77	    bars s..k, s in [k-W+1, k-mmin+1] (windows of at least mmin bars). Returns (max t, length of the maximising window).
78	    Sums are accumulated from the shortest window outwards, so every window's regression uses exactly its own bars."""
79	    i0 = k - W + 1
80	    if i0 < 0: i0 = 0
81	    ny = k - i0 + 1
82	    if ny < mmin: return NAN, NAN
83	    base = logc[i0]
84	    xtx = np.zeros((4, 4)); xty = np.zeros(4); yty = 0.0
85	    best = -1e300; bestlen = NAN
86	    nrows = 0
87	    for s in range(ny - 4, -1, -1):
88	        t = s + 3                                           # the row added when the window starts at s

111	@njit(cache=True)
112	def cusum_filter(r, h):
113	    """Symmetric CUSUM filter on returns r with a per-bar threshold h_t (NaN threshold: no event possible). Returns the event flag."""
114	    n = r.shape[0]; ev = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
115	    sp = 0.0; sn = 0.0
116	    for t in range(n):
117	        x = r[t]
118	        if x != x: continue
119	        sp = max(0.0, sp + x); sn = min(0.0, sn + x)
120	        ht = h[t]
121	        if ht != ht: continue
122	        if sp > ht or sn < -ht:
123	            ev[t] = 1; sp = 0.0; sn = 0.0
124	    return ev

127	@njit(cache=True)
128	def events_window_and_since(ev, win):
129	    """Events in (t-win, t] and bars since the last event (NaN before the first)."""
130	    n = ev.shape[0]; cnt = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64); since = np.full(n, NAN)
131	    cs = np.cumsum(ev); last = -1
132	    for t in range(n):
133	        lo = t - win
134	        cnt[t] = cs[t] - (cs[lo] if lo >= 0 else 0)
135	        if ev[t] > 0: last = t

140	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Chu-Stinchcombe-White (AFML 17.4.1) on the session's levels
141	@njit(cache=True)
142	def csw_at(logc, k, s0, b_alpha):
143	    """S_{n,t} = (y_t - y_n) / (sigma_t sqrt(t - n)) for n in [s0, t-1], sigma_t^2 = mean of the session's squared level changes
144	    up to t; critical value c = sqrt(b_alpha + log(t - n)). Returns (max |S|, max (|S| - c), sign of y_t - y_n at that argmax)."""
145	    t = k
146	    if t - s0 < 2: return NAN, NAN, NAN
147	    ss = 0.0
148	    for j in range(s0 + 1, t + 1):
149	        d = logc[j] - logc[j - 1]; ss += d * d
150	    var = ss / (t - s0)
151	    if var <= 0: return NAN, NAN, NAN
152	    sig = math.sqrt(var)
153	    best_abs = -1.0; best_ex = -1e300; sgn = 0.0
154	    for n_ in range(s0, t):
155	        S = (logc[t] - logc[n_]) / (sig * math.sqrt(t - n_))
156	        a = abs(S); c = math.sqrt(b_alpha + math.log(t - n_)); ex = a - c
157	        if a > best_abs: best_abs = a
158	        if ex > best_ex:
159	            best_ex = ex; sgn = 1.0 if S > 0 else (-1.0 if S < 0 else 0.0)
160	    return best_abs, best_ex, sgn

163	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BOCPD (Adams & MacKay 2007), normal-inverse-gamma / Student-t predictive
164	@njit(cache=True)
165	def bocpd(x, hazard, rmax, mu0, kappa0, alpha0, beta0):
166	    """Run-length posterior over 0..rmax (mass beyond rmax folded into the rmax bin, whose sufficient statistics keep updating).
167	    Returns per bar: MAP run length, P(run length < 10), bars since the last MAP reset (a reset = the MAP run length fell)."""
168	    n = x.shape[0]; R = np.zeros(rmax + 1); R[0] = 1.0; Rn = np.zeros(rmax + 1)
169	    mu = np.full(rmax + 1, mu0); be = np.full(rmax + 1, beta0)
170	    mun = np.empty(rmax + 1); ben = np.empty(rmax + 1)
171	    kap = np.empty(rmax + 1); al = np.empty(rmax + 1); c = np.empty(rmax + 1); nu = np.empty(rmax + 1)
172	    for r in range(rmax + 1):
173	        kap[r] = kappa0 + r; al[r] = alpha0 + 0.5 * r; nu[r] = 2.0 * al[r]
174	        c[r] = math.lgamma(0.5 * (nu[r] + 1.0)) - math.lgamma(0.5 * nu[r]) - 0.5 * math.log(nu[r] * math.pi)
175	    pred = np.empty(rmax + 1)
176	    map_rl = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64); p_lt10 = np.full(n, NAN); since = np.full(n, NAN)
177	    last_reset = -1; prev_map = 0
178	    for t in range(n):
179	        xt = x[t]
180	        if xt != xt:                                        # no observation: carry the state, repeat the features
181	            map_rl[t] = prev_map; p_lt10[t] = p_lt10[t - 1] if t > 0 else NAN
182	            if last_reset >= 0: since[t] = t - last_reset
183	            continue
184	        for r in range(rmax + 1):
185	            sc2 = be[r] * (kap[r] + 1.0) / (al[r] * kap[r])
186	            z = (xt - mu[r]); z = z * z / (nu[r] * sc2)
187	            pred[r] = math.exp(c[r] - 0.5 * math.log(sc2) - 0.5 * (nu[r] + 1.0) * math.log1p(z))
188	        cp = 0.0
189	        for r in range(rmax + 1): Rn[r] = 0.0
190	        for r in range(rmax + 1):
191	            pr = R[r] * pred[r]; cp += pr * hazard
192	            if r < rmax: Rn[r + 1] += pr * (1.0 - hazard)
193	            else: Rn[rmax] += pr * (1.0 - hazard)
194	        Rn[0] = cp
195	        tot = 0.0
196	        for r in range(rmax + 1): tot += Rn[r]
197	        if tot <= 0:
198	            for r in range(rmax + 1): Rn[r] = 0.0
199	            Rn[0] = 1.0; tot = 1.0
200	        for r in range(rmax + 1): Rn[r] /= tot
201	        # sufficient statistics: bin r+1 <- bin r updated with x; bin 0 <- prior; bin rmax <- mass-weighted average of the two
202	        mun[0] = mu0; ben[0] = beta0
203	        for r in range(rmax):
204	            mun[r + 1] = (kap[r] * mu[r] + xt) / (kap[r] + 1.0)
205	            ben[r + 1] = be[r] + kap[r] * (xt - mu[r]) * (xt - mu[r]) / (2.0 * (kap[r] + 1.0))
206	        mu_self = (kap[rmax] * mu[rmax] + xt) / (kap[rmax] + 1.0)
207	        be_self = be[rmax] + kap[rmax] * (xt - mu[rmax]) * (xt - mu[rmax]) / (2.0 * (kap[rmax] + 1.0))
208	        w1 = R[rmax - 1] * pred[rmax - 1]; w2 = R[rmax] * pred[rmax]
209	        if w1 + w2 > 0:
210	            mun[rmax] = (w1 * mun[rmax] + w2 * mu_self) / (w1 + w2); ben[rmax] = (w1 * ben[rmax] + w2 * be_self) / (w1 + w2)
211	        for r in range(rmax + 1):
212	            R[r] = Rn[r]; mu[r] = mun[r]; be[r] = ben[r]
213	        m = 0; bestp = -1.0; p10 = 0.0
214	        for r in range(rmax + 1):
215	            if R[r] > bestp: bestp = R[r]; m = r
216	            if r < 10: p10 += R[r]
217	        map_rl[t] = m; p_lt10[t] = p10
218	        if t > 0 and m < prev_map: last_reset = t
219	        if last_reset >= 0: since[t] = t - last_reset
220	        prev_map = m
221	    return map_rl, p_lt10, since

225	@njit(cache=True)
226	def event_counts(n, ev_bar, ev_is_bos):

240	@njit(cache=True)
241	def session_windows(high, low, close, open_, atr, session_bar, ev_at, N):
242	    """Same-session windows of N bars ending at t: events in the window, (max high - min low) / atr_t, (close_t - close_{t-N} or
243	    the session open when t-N is before the session) / atr_t."""
244	    n = close.shape[0]
245	    evN = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64); rngN = np.full(n, NAN); retN = np.full(n, NAN)
246	    for t in range(n):
247	        s0 = t - session_bar[t]
248	        lo = t - N + 1
249	        if lo < s0: lo = s0
250	        hi_ = -1e300; lo_ = 1e300; e = 0
251	        for j in range(lo, t + 1):
252	            if high[j] > hi_: hi_ = high[j]
253	            if low[j] < lo_: lo_ = low[j]
254	            e += ev_at[j]
255	        evN[t] = e
256	        a = atr[t]
257	        if a > 0:
258	            rngN[t] = (hi_ - lo_) / a
259	            ref = close[t - N] if t - N >= s0 else open_[s0]
260	            retN[t] = (close[t] - ref) / a
261	    return evN, rngN, retN

264	@njit(cache=True)
265	def window_summaries(high, low, close, r, atr, session_bar, ks, sg, L):
266	    """At SETUP bars ks with direction sg: sign-agreement count of the last 10 bar returns with sg (tape bars, gap-free returns),
267	    drawdown from the same-session L-bar window extreme against the direction in ATR, OLS slope of (high-low)/atr_k over the window."""
268	    m = ks.shape[0]; agree = np.full(m, NAN); dd = np.full(m, NAN); slope = np.full(m, NAN)
269	    for q in range(m):
270	        k = ks[q]; s = sg[q]
271	        c = 0
272	        for j in range(max(0, k - 9), k + 1):
273	            if (s > 0 and r[j] > 0) or (s < 0 and r[j] < 0): c += 1
274	        agree[q] = c
275	        s0 = k - session_bar[k]; lo = k - L + 1
276	        if lo < s0: lo = s0
277	        a = atr[k]
278	        if a <= 0: continue
279	        hi_ = -1e300; lo_ = 1e300; n = 0; sx = 0.0; sy = 0.0; sxx = 0.0; sxy = 0.0
280	        for j in range(lo, k + 1):
281	            if high[j] > hi_: hi_ = high[j]
282	            if low[j] < lo_: lo_ = low[j]
283	            x = float(j - lo); y = (high[j] - low[j]) / a
284	            n += 1; sx += x; sy += y; sxx += x * x; sxy += x * y
285	        dd[q] = (hi_ - close[k]) / a if s > 0 else (close[k] - lo_) / a
286	        if n >= 3:
287	            den = n * sxx - sx * sx
288	            if den > 0: slope[q] = (n * sxy - sx * sy) / den
289	    return agree, dd, slope

292	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- state models: HMM forward filter, jump model DP
293	@njit(cache=True)
294	def hmm_forward_filter(Z, startprob, transmat, means, variances):
295	    """Scaled forward filter of a diagonal-Gaussian HMM: P(s_t | x_{<=t}) for every bar (never the smoothed posterior)."""
296	    n, p = Z.shape; K = means.shape[0]
297	    post = np.empty((n, K)); alpha = np.empty(K); tmp = np.empty(K)
298	    logdet = np.empty(K)
299	    for s in range(K):
300	        v = 0.0
301	        for j in range(p): v += math.log(2.0 * math.pi * variances[s, j])
302	        logdet[s] = -0.5 * v
303	    loglik = 0.0
304	    for t in range(n):
305	        # emission log densities, shifted by their max for stability
306	        mx = -1e300
307	        for s in range(K):
308	            e = logdet[s]
309	            for j in range(p):
310	                d = Z[t, j] - means[s, j]; e -= 0.5 * d * d / variances[s, j]
311	            tmp[s] = e
312	            if e > mx: mx = e
313	        tot = 0.0
314	        for s in range(K):
315	            if t == 0: pr = startprob[s]
316	            else:
317	                pr = 0.0
318	                for u in range(K): pr += post[t - 1, u] * transmat[u, s]
319	            alpha[s] = pr * math.exp(tmp[s] - mx); tot += alpha[s]
320	        if tot <= 0:
321	            for s in range(K): alpha[s] = 1.0 / K
322	            tot = 1.0
323	        for s in range(K): post[t, s] = alpha[s] / tot
324	        loglik += math.log(tot) + mx
325	    return post, loglik

328	@njit(cache=True)
329	def jump_viterbi(Z, C, lam):
330	    """Offline DP for the statistical jump model on a fitted window: argmin over paths of sum ||x_t - c_{s_t}||^2 + lam 1[s_t != s_{t-1}]."""
331	    n, p = Z.shape; K = C.shape[0]
332	    V = np.empty((n, K)); B = np.zeros((n, K), dtype=np.int64)
333	    for s in range(K):
334	        d = 0.0
335	        for j in range(p): dd = Z[0, j] - C[s, j]; d += dd * dd
336	        V[0, s] = d
337	    for t in range(1, n):
338	        mn = 1e300; arg = 0
339	        for u in range(K):
340	            if V[t - 1, u] < mn: mn = V[t - 1, u]; arg = u
341	        for s in range(K):
342	            stay = V[t - 1, s]; sw = mn + lam
343	            if stay <= sw: prev = s; base = stay
344	            else: prev = arg; base = sw
345	            d = 0.0
346	            for j in range(p): dd = Z[t, j] - C[s, j]; d += dd * dd
347	            V[t, s] = base + d; B[t, s] = prev
348	    states = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
349	    mn = 1e300; arg = 0
350	    for s in range(K):
351	        if V[n - 1, s] < mn: mn = V[n - 1, s]; arg = s
352	    states[n - 1] = arg
353	    for t in range(n - 1, 0, -1): states[t - 1] = B[t, states[t]]
354	    return states, mn
355

357	@njit(cache=True)
358	def jump_online(Z, C, lam):
359	    """Online prefix state: s_t = argmin_s V_t(s) with V_t(s) = min_u (V_{t-1}(u) + lam 1[s != u]) + ||x_t - c_s||^2 (bars <= t only)."""
360	    n, p = Z.shape; K = C.shape[0]
361	    Vp = np.zeros(K); Vn = np.empty(K); states = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
362	    for t in range(n):
363	        mn = 1e300
364	        for u in range(K):
365	            if Vp[u] < mn: mn = Vp[u]
366	        for s in range(K):
367	            if t == 0: base = 0.0
368	            elif Vp[s] <= mn + lam: base = Vp[s]
369	            else: base = mn + lam
370	            d = 0.0
371	            for j in range(p): dd = Z[t, j] - C[s, j]; d += dd * dd
372	            Vn[s] = base + d
373	        mn2 = 1e300; arg = 0
374	        for s in range(K):
375	            if Vn[s] < mn2: mn2 = Vn[s]; arg = s
376	        states[t] = arg
377	        for s in range(K): Vp[s] = Vn[s] - mn2
378	    return states
379

381	@njit(cache=True)
382	def run_length_of(states):
383	    """Consecutive bars (ending at t) with the same state as at t (>= 1)."""
384	    n = states.shape[0]; out = np.ones(n, dtype=np.int64)
385	    for t in range(1, n):
386	        out[t] = out[t - 1] + 1 if states[t] == states[t - 1] else 1
387	    return out

22	         same_setup_keys=bool(np.array_equal(full_pre.setup_i.to_numpy(), trunc.setup_i.to_numpy())), tolerance=TOL, columns={}, dropped=[], kept=[])
23	assert R["same_setup_keys"], "the truncated build must contain exactly the SETUPs before the cut"

1	# FZ v3 design panel (2026-09-29)
2	
3	Three designers (quant-ML canon, sequence / representation learning, decision-making / RL) proposed studies for the FZ v3 program; two judges (feasibility-and-rigour, skeptical practitioner) scored each on feasible_here / rigour / expected_value (0-5) with keep = all three >= 3. Generated from the workflow result; the judges' fixes are part of the program. Feasibility was scored against the local 4-core box; in the cloud the compute ceilings do not apply, the rigour and overfitting fixes do.

28	## Judges' verdicts
29	
30	### Judge 1
31	
32	Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.
33	
34	Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
35	
36	Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.
37	
38	Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.
39	
40	### Judge 2
41	
42	Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.

46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.

48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).

52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.

54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.

60	## Studies

84	### deep-sequence-regime-states (priority 2)
85	
86	**technique.** Latent regime states from per-bar features: a hand-rolled Gaussian HMM (Baum-Welch, causal forward filtering at inference), a statistical jump model (k-means with a jump penalty, online prefix version), a GaussianMixture no-dynamics baseline, and Bayesian online change-point detection (BOCPD) run-length features; all fit on IS bars only.
87	
88	**what_it_answers.** Is there a machine-found 'chop' state that marks losing Foundation SETUPs better than the hand rule H2 tests (n_choch_since_bos >= k), how many bars of confirmation it needs (the filtered state lags), and whether 'time since the last structural change' (BOCPD run length) carries the same information more cheaply. Also gives the vision study (below) a mechanical comparator.
89	
90	**method.** Per-bar as-of feature vector x_t from fz_v3/<tf>/bars.csv and events.csv: |log return|, (high-low)/atr14, |close-open|/(high-low), log(volume/median volume of the previous 20 bars), events (BOS+CHoCH) in the last 36 bars, CHoCHs since the last BOS at t, range of the last 36 bars / atr14, signed 36-bar return / atr14; features are z-scored with IS statistics. Models: (a) Gaussian HMM with K in {3,4}, diagonal covariance, Baum-Welch 50 iterations in numba, initialised from k-means, fit on IS bars of the training folds; at inference only the forward (filtered) posterior P(s_t | x_<=t) is used; the smoothed posterior is computed too but only as a hindsight diagnostic. (b) Statistical jump model: minimise sum ||x_t - mu_{s_t}||^2 + lambda * 1[s_t != s_{t-1}] by alternating centroid updates and Viterbi DP, lambda from a small grid chosen on CV; the online state is the prefix-DP argmax. (c) sklearn GaussianMixture(K) on the same vectors as the no-dynamics baseline. (d) BOCPD (Adams & MacKay) with a normal-inverse-gamma predictive on 1m/5m log returns and separately on log range, hazard 1/H for H in {60, 240} bars, run-length truncated at 400; features: MAP run length, P(run length < 10), bars since the last MAP reset. At each SETUP bar k the study attaches: P(state = c | x_<=k) for each state, the jump-model state, and the BOCPD features. Analysis: Foundation net and win rate by filtered state and by BOCPD run-length bucket on IS; identify the state with the worst expectancy (the candidate chop state) inside each training fold; gate = skip when P(chop) >= tau (tau grid 0.5..0.9) or run length >= r; evaluate on purged session-blocked CV against H2's rule at matched skip fraction (the HMM must beat the hand rule's kept-vs-skipped difference at the same trade count, else it is not worth its parameters); final model refit on all IS; OOS once. Outputs: state description tables (means per feature), transition matrix, the expectancy-by-state table on IS CV and OOS, the control percentile, and the distilled rule.
91	
92	**leakage_controls.** Only filtered (forward) posteriors and prefix-DP states are used at SETUP bars; smoothed posteriors and full-sequence Viterbi paths are labelled hindsight and never enter a feature; all model parameters and z-scoring statistics are estimated on IS training-fold bars only, refit per fold; BOCPD is causal by construction; the chop state is identified per training fold, not on the test fold; embargo covers the longest Foundation hold; OOS bars are only ever filtered through the frozen IS model.
93	
94	**compute.** 5m: HMM 76k bars x 8 features x 4 states x 50 EM iterations in numba ~1 min per fold, 5 folds ~5 min; 1m 445k bars ~5 min per fold, ~25 min; jump model similar; GMM ~1 min per fit (benchmarked 51 s for 90k x 6 x 4 components); BOCPD 445k x 400 run lengths in numba ~1 min. Total ~40-60 CPU-minutes per timeframe; peak memory under 400 MB (bars as float32, per-bar posteriors K x N float32).
95	
96	**libraries.** numpy, numba (HMM forward/backward, jump-model DP, BOCPD), sklearn.mixture.GaussianMixture and sklearn.cluster.KMeans for initialisation, pandas.
97	
98	**output_as_config.** Preferred: a distilled rule list over scalar as-of features that reproduces the chop-state gate (a depth-3 tree fit to predict 'P(chop) >= tau' from the same per-bar features must reach >= 85% fidelity on CV, else the study says the state is not expressible compactly). Alternative needing a user decision: an fz block key such as {"regime": {"model": "hmm_filtered", "features": [...], "means": [[...]], "vars": [[...]], "transition": [[...]], "chop_state": 2, "skip_if_p_chop_ge": 0.7}} (about 40-60 numbers for K=4 x 8 features) plus a forward-filter routine in fz code; the BOCPD variant is two numbers (hazard, run-length threshold) and is compact by itself.
99	
100	**novelty.** Markov-switching regimes (Hamilton 1989) and Gaussian HMMs (Rabiner 1989) are classical; the current pieces are statistical jump models for regime detection with an online variant (Bemporad et al. 2018; Nystrup, Kolm & Lindstrom 2020/2021, 'sparse jump models'), Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay 2007) as a causal alternative to offline change-point search (ruptures, Truong et al. 2020), and the discipline of separating filtered from smoothed states (the look-ahead trap in regime backtests documented by Nystrup et al.).
101	
102	**Judge 1** feasible 4 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: a Gaussian HMM on |return|, range/ATR and event counts finds volatility states, not the user's chop; the 'worst-expectancy state' is picked per fold from K states (label switching plus selection), the filtered posterior lags 10-30 bars at 1m, and the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features, at which point the HMM added nothing but trials. Fix: run only BOCPD (two numbers, causal, one minute) and hand run-length features to study 3; run the HMM only if study 3 shows the H2 counts are not already the regime cluster, and then on 5m only.
103	
104	**Judge 2** feasible 4 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: hmmlearn is absent, so Baum-Welch with scaling is hand-coded in numba (~150 lines, real bug risk): run the cheap rungs first, BOCPD (2-number config, numba, ~1 min) and sklearn GaussianMixture (benchmarked 51 s), and fit the HMM/jump model only if the GMM state already shows a kept-vs-skipped signal at matched skip fraction versus n_choch_since_bos on CV. Emit the state posteriors and BOCPD run length as candidate features to the importance study rather than running an own tau grid. The 40-60-number HMM config plus a forward filter in fz code is a new key type: record it as a user decision and ship only the distilled rule if fidelity >= 85%. 1m HMM is ~25 min per model set at < 400 MB, acceptable now; 5m first.

106	### deep-sequence-rocket-probe (priority 3)
107	
108	**technique.** Random convolutional kernel transform (MiniRocket-style: thousands of fixed dilated 1D kernels, proportion-of-positive-values pooling) over the multichannel pre-SETUP bar window, then a ridge/logistic linear probe; compared with an sklearn MLP on the same window and with the H5 tabular gradient-boosting reference; then distilled to rules.
109	
110	**what_it_answers.** Whether the shape of the last 60-120 bars (1m) / 12-36 bars (5m) before a SETUP carries any information about the Foundation outcome beyond the hand-built as-of features; how large the ceiling is (AUC and kept-vs-skipped expectancy at fixed skip fractions); and whether the part that matters can be written as a few threshold rules on scalar features.
111	
112	**method.** Window tensor per SETUP: L bars ending at setup_i inclusive (1m: L in {60, 120}; 5m: L in {12, 36}), channels: sg x log return per bar (direction-normalised so up and down SETUPs pool), (high-low)/atr14[k], sg x (close-open)/atr14[k], log(volume/vol_med20[k]) with NA -> 0 plus an NA flag channel, sg x (close - choch_lvl)/atr14[k], and a same-session indicator; stored float32. Transform: 5,000-10,000 random kernels of length 9, weights in {-1, 2} centred, dilations sampled log-uniformly up to L/4, one channel or a random pair per kernel, bias drawn from quantiles of the training-fold convolution outputs (as MiniRocket does), PPV pooling (numba, benchmarked 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels x 60 bars). Probes: RidgeClassifierCV on the PPV features (alpha grid 1e-3..1e3), L2 logistic regression for calibrated probabilities, and ridge regression on winsorised net (+-10,000 INR). Comparators inside the same CV folds: sklearn MLPClassifier(64,16) on the flattened z-scored window, H5's xgboost on tabular as-of features, and the stacked model (tabular + top PCA components of the PPV features). Selection on 5-fold purged session-blocked IS CV by: AUC, mean net of the kept set at skip fractions 30/50/70%, kept-vs-skipped difference, and the pooled session-matched control percentile of the kept set; incremental value = stacked minus tabular. Distillation: the probe score's bottom tercile ('predicted loser') becomes a binary target and a depth-3 decision tree on scalar as-of features (tabular + a handful of window summaries such as the sign-agreement count of the last 10 bars, the drawdown from the window high, the bar-range trend) is fit to it; the tree's rules are the config candidate if fidelity >= 85% and the rule's own CV kept-vs-skipped difference keeps >= 70% of the probe's. Final: refit on all IS, one OOS run. Outputs: the CV/OOS table for each model, calibration plot data, the distilled rules, and the statement of how much of the effect the rules keep.
113	
114	**leakage_controls.** Windows end at the SETUP bar; kernel biases, channel scaling and PCA are fit on training folds only, inside the CV loop; labels (fnd_net_inr) never enter the transform; purged/embargoed session-blocked CV; the number of window lengths x kernel counts x probes tried is recorded and a max-T permutation over that family is reported; OOS once with the frozen kernel set (seeds logged) and frozen ridge weights. Direction-normalisation is stated per channel so that no channel silently encodes a forward quantity.
115	
116	**compute.** Transform: 5,326 windows x 6 channels x 120 bars x 10,000 kernels ~90 s (+21 s JIT) per fold-fit of biases; RidgeCV on 5,326 x 10,000 ~2-5 min per fit; 5 folds x 2 window lengths x 3 probes ~45-75 CPU-minutes for 1m, ~10 min for 5m; MLP comparator ~5 min. Peak memory ~600 MB (feature matrix 5,326 x 10,000 float32 = 213 MB, doubled by sklearn's float64 copy; use 5,000 kernels if the lab rebuild is still holding memory).
117	
118	**libraries.** numpy, numba (kernel transform), sklearn (RidgeClassifierCV, LogisticRegression, MLPClassifier, DecisionTreeClassifier, PCA), xgboost for the H5 comparator, shap optional for the stacked model's attribution.
119	
120	**output_as_config.** Only the distilled rule list is proposed for ST13/ST14 (<= 8 rules of depth <= 3 over as-of scalar features, provenance 'distilled from rocket probe, script deep_rocket.py, sha'); the kernel bank and ridge weights (~10k numbers) are not compact and are explicitly not offered as config. If the probe shows a ceiling the rules cannot reach, the study reports the gap in INR/trade and stops.
121	
122	**novelty.** ROCKET (Dempster, Petitjean & Webb, DMKD 2020), MiniRocket (KDD 2021), MultiRocket (2022) and Hydra (2023) are the current state of the art for small-data time-series classification on CPU and descend from random-feature methods (Rahimi & Recht 2007) and untrained convolutional features; the linear-probe evaluation protocol is SimCLR's (Chen et al. 2020). It is the honest substitute for a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer on a box with no deep-learning framework and 4.5k labelled sequences.
123	
124	**Judge 1** feasible 3 · rigour 3 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: RidgeClassifierCV picks alpha by an internal leave-one-out that is not session-blocked, so 10,000 PPV features on ~3,600 windows fit within-session neighbours; every pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition (CHoCH then continuation), so shape 'motifs' are the rule, not information; the shippable form is again a scalar-feature tree, so at best it reports an unreachable ceiling. Fix: if run at all, 5m only, 2,000 kernels, one window length, alpha chosen by nested GroupKFold, and a pre-registered stop (stacked minus tabular AUC < 0.02 in every fold = report and stop); it never gets a candidate slot and its trials still go to the ledger.
125	
126	**Judge 2** feasible 3 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: As proposed (10,000 kernels, 5,326 x 10,000 float32 doubled to float64 by RidgeCV, ~600 MB peak, 45-75 CPU-min) it does not fit beside lab.py at 1.24 GB with 759 MB free, and the prior that 4.5k labelled 60-bar windows beat hand features in intraday index futures is low. Reduce to a single ceiling check: 1m only, L=60, 2,000 kernels (43 MB matrix, RidgeCV in seconds), one probe, harness splitter; if the CPCV 5th-percentile AUC gain over the tabular HGB is < 0.03 the study ends with that number. The distilled window summaries (sign-agreement count, drawdown from window high) can still be offered to the importance study as scalar features.

128	### deep-sequence-vision-labels (priority 4)
129	
130	**technique.** Multimodal Claude as a hindsight annotator: rendered IS session charts labelled sideways / trending per hour-bin by vision, with a reliability check; the labels are ground truth for (a) a direct test that sideways hurts Foundation SETUPs and (b) a causal detector distilled into rules.
131

150	### deep-sequence-motif-shapelet (priority 5)
151	
152	**technique.** SETUP-anchored matrix-profile motif discovery (MASS/FFT z-normalised distances), time-series clustering of pre-SETUP shapes (k-means on z-normalised windows and on random-kernel features), and discriminative shapelet search; plus a causal novelty score (distance of the pre-SETUP window to the nearest earlier window on the tape).
153	
154	**what_it_answers.** Whether recurring pre-SETUP shapes exist (motifs), whether any motif or cluster has a Foundation expectancy that survives a session-blocked permutation test, whether a single short template (a shapelet) with a distance threshold separates losers, and whether 'this looks like nothing seen before' (novelty) or 'this looks exactly like a familiar pattern' predicts the outcome.
155	
156	**method.** Windows: the direction-normalised close path over the last m bars ending at setup_i (1m: m in {30, 60}; 5m: m in {12, 24}), z-normalised per window; a second representation is the 6-channel tensor of the rocket study. Motifs (deep_motif.py): full pairwise z-normalised Euclidean distance matrix among IS SETUP windows (4,502^2 x 60, seconds via matmul), nearest-neighbour graph, motif chains and agglomerative clustering with a distance cut chosen by the silhouette on training folds; per-cluster Foundation net, win rate, n, and a permutation p where the null shuffles labels within session blocks; clusters with n < 40 are reported but never proposed. Clustering (deep_cluster.py): k-means (k in 4..12) on the z-normalised paths and separately on the PPV features; cluster expectancy tables on CV (the cluster assignment for a test-fold SETUP uses training-fold centroids only); 'loser clusters' are then explained by a depth-3 tree on scalar as-of features (fidelity reported). 239	
240	**technique.** Clustered feature importance (MDA and MDI on correlation clusters, single-feature importance per cluster) under purged cross-validation, the orthogonal-feature sanity check, fractional differentiation (fixed-width FFD with a hand-coded ADF choice of d*) as a candidate feature family, and TreeSHAP interaction values for discovering the 2-3-feature interactions that justify depth-2/3 rules.
241	
242	**what_it_answers.** Which of the 143 as-of columns (97 numeric, 114 pairs with |rho| > 0.9, so raw importances would be split by substitution) carry information about the intraday Foundation outcome; which at most 8 feature clusters the ST13/ST14 keys should be built from and what their config-expressible representative is; whether the canon's fractionally differentiated price features add anything beyond the ATR-normalised distances already in the table; which feature pairs interact strongly enough to justify a depth-2/3 rule, so that H5's rule search can be restricted (fewer trials, lower PBO).
243	
244	**method.** (1) Feature set: as-of numeric plus encoded categoricals as in the meta-label study; NaN kept for HGB, a missing-indicator plus median for bagging; columns with > 40% NaN dropped and listed. (2) FFD family: on log close per timeframe, fixed-width fractional differentiation for d in {0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0} with weight cut 1e-4 (window length recorded); ADF regression with constant and 2 lags hand-coded in numpy (MacKinnon 5% critical value -2.86 embedded and cited); d* = smallest d whose ADF statistic on IS bars is below the critical value; features at the SETUP bar: ffd_close_d*, its z-score against a 60-bar rolling std, the same on log volume; plus the CUSUM-filter counts from the regime study when available. (3) Clustering: Spearman correlation on IS, distance sqrt(0.5 (1 - rho)), scipy average linkage, cut chosen by silhouette in the 20-40 cluster range; every cluster gets a representative chosen by config-expressibility (integer counts and card fields before ATR ratios before raw points). (4) Model and protocol: BaggingClassifier of depth-limited trees on the L1 label with |net| weights under the harness splitter (12 purged, embargoed blocks). Clustered MDA: permute all features of a cluster jointly on the test fold, 5 permutations x 12 folds, record the drop in OOF weighted log-loss and, separately, the drop in OOF kept-vs-skipped expectancy at the fold's tau (the metric that matters); report mean and std across folds; a cluster is kept only when its mean MDA exceeds one std. (5) Orthogonal check: PCA on standardised IS features, weighted Kendall tau between MDI rank and eigenvalue rank; a low tau is reported as a warning that the importance may be noise-fitting. (6) Interactions: xgboost max_depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05 on the same folds restricted to the top-40 features; shap.TreeExplainer(...).shap_interaction_values on OOF rows; pairs ranked by mean |interaction|; the top 5 pairs with their split points from the tree structure become candidate depth-2/3 rules for H5 and the distillation step. 260	### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)
261	
262	**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.
263	
264	**what_it_answers.** The user's acceptance criterion made formal: can SETUPs be skipped with a finite-sample guarantee that at most alpha of the true winners are skipped (marginally over SETUPs, under exchangeability), what skip rate, loser recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy each alpha buys on IS out-of-fold, whether the winner coverage holds on OOS, what the hour-of-day guarantee costs in sample size, and how far a coverage-chosen threshold sits from the expectancy-chosen threshold of the meta-label study.
265	
266	**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.
267	
268	**leakage_controls.** Scores are out-of-fold from the purged, embargoed splitter; the conformal quantile uses only winners from calibration folds; alpha, the time bins and the selection rule are fixed before OOS; ACI's state carries forward without any OOS tuning; the study reads no OOS row until the single frozen run; the comparison with the expectancy-chosen tau is on IS-OOF only.

270	**compute.** Quantiles over <= 5k scores x 5 alphas x 12 folds and a sequential ACI loop over <= 5k rows: under 1 CPU-minute, under 100 MB; it depends only on the meta-label study's OOF file.

282	### quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing (priority 5)
283	
284	**technique.** Probability calibration on purged out-of-fold predictions (isotonic and Platt, nested), expected-net sizing under the asymmetric payoff (Kelly fraction with class-conditional mean win and loss) discretised to 0-3 lots, compared with AFML's symmetric z-score sizing, judged with a lot-aware extension of the session-matched random control.
285	
286	**what_it_answers.** Given a calibrated p_win and the asymmetric payoff (5m IS: 22% winners, win mean +10,878 INR, loss mean -3,429 INR, top-decile winners 46% of gross wins), how many lots per SETUP, whether sizing adds expectancy per lot beyond the skip decision, whether the calibration is real (reliability curve, Brier skill against the 22% base rate, ECE) on IS-OOF and once on OOS, and whether the honest answer with 181 winners is simply 'one lot or skip'.
287	
288	**method.** Calibration: sklearn IsotonicRegression (and Platt via LogisticRegression as the low-variance alternative) fitted on the meta-label study's IS OOF p_hat against the L1 label, nested inside the harness splitter (fit on 11 folds' OOF, apply to the 12th); reliability curves in 5 quantile bins, Brier score and Brier skill score versus the base rate, expected calibration error, per model (scorecard is the deployable one).
